digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III; Pakia (2005) App. VI

teaser.en: Its name means 'drum maker': the soft, light trunk of this scarlet-flowered tree is hollowed out to make drum bodies.

summary.en: *Mwamba ngoma* is a thorny coral tree of the coastal bush and forest, with three-part leaves and bright scarlet flowers. Its soft, light wood gives the Digo drum bodies, and its name says so.

about.en:
*Mwamba ngoma* is a thorny tree in the bean family, related to the coral trees found across Africa. Each leaf is made of three broad leaflets, and the branches carry prickles. When it flowers, the tree is hung with clusters of vivid scarlet blooms, shaped like the narrow, curved flowers typical of coral trees, which are a favourite of sunbirds.

The wood is the thing to know about. It is soft and light, easy to cut and carve, which is just what a drum maker wants and what most builders do not.

where.en: Look for it in coastal bushland, open woodland and the edges of coastal forest. It is easiest to spot when it is in flower, when the red clusters stand out against the green and grey of the bush.

uses.en: The trunk is hollowed out to make drum bodies. Because the wood is light and works easily, a section of stem can be carved and emptied into a shell, ready to be covered with skin.

culture.en: The name *mwamba ngoma* is read as 'drum maker' (from *ngoma*, drum), and it ties the tree directly to the music of the coast. Drums are at the heart of Digo dances and gatherings, so this is a tree whose wood has long been heard as well as seen.

names.en: The Digo name is *mwamba ngoma*, also written *mbamba ngoma*. The same name is used in Swahili. No English common name is in wide use; botanists call it *Erythrina sacleuxii*. The Mgombato dictionary gives *mwambangoma* as a different tree, the desert date (*Balanites aegyptiaca*), with the Swahili *mchunju*, so the name may cover more than one tree, or the sources may disagree.

reason.en: Black mangrove whose hollow trunks are also made into drums
Grey mangrove also used for drums
Another coastal tree used for drums
A Balanites; the dictionary links the name mwambangoma to that genus
